questions.questionText: Which of the following Venn diagrams best represents the relationship among: "Musicians", "Violinists", and "Instrumentalists"?
questions.optionB: Two intersecting circles completely outside the third circle
questions.optionC: Violinists and Musicians intersecting, with Instrumentalists disjoint
questions.optionD: Three concentric circles with Violinists innermost, Instrumentalists in middle, and Musicians outermost
questions.explanation: All violinists are instrumentalists (since the violin is an instrument), and all instrumentalists are musicians. Thus, Violinists is a subset of Instrumentalists, which in turn is a subset of Musicians. This is represented by three concentric circles.

questions.questionText: In a college class of 100 students, 60 play Cricket, 50 play Football, and 20 play both sports. How many students play neither Cricket nor Football?
questions.explanation: Using the formula: n(C union F) = n(C) + n(F) - n(C intersect F) = 60 + 50 - 20 = 90 students play at least one sport. The number of students playing neither sport = Total - n(C union F) = 100 - 90 = 10 students.

questions.questionText: Which Venn diagram best illustrates the relationship among: "Doctors", "Smokers", and "Females"?
questions.optionA: Two disjoint circles inside a third large circle
questions.optionB: Three mutually intersecting circles overlapping at a common central region
questions.optionD: One circle containing two other intersecting circles
questions.explanation: Some doctors are females, some doctors are smokers, and some female doctors smoke. Thus, each category partially overlaps with the other two, represented by three intersecting circles with a common central region.

questions.questionText: In a survey of 120 people, 70 drink Tea, 60 drink Coffee, and 15 drink neither beverage. How many people drink both Tea and Coffee?
questions.explanation: Total drinking at least one beverage = 120 - 15 = 105. Formula: n(T union C) = n(T) + n(C) - n(T intersect C). 105 = 70 + 60 - Both => 105 = 130 - Both => Both = 130 - 105 = 25 people.

questions.questionText: Which of the following geometric figures best represents the relationship among: "Mammals", "Dogs", and "Cats"?
questions.optionD: A large circle containing two separate, non-overlapping circles inside it
questions.explanation: Both Dogs and Cats are Mammals (subsets of Mammals), but no dog is a cat (Dogs and Cats are completely disjoint). This is represented by a large enclosing circle with two separate non-overlapping circles inside.

questions.questionText: In a group of 80 IT professionals, 45 know Python, 40 know Java, and 15 know both languages. How many professionals know ONLY Python?
questions.explanation: Number of professionals knowing ONLY Python = Total Python - Both = 45 - 15 = 30 professionals.

questions.questionText: Which Venn diagram correctly represents the relationship among: "States", "Districts", and "Cities"?
questions.optionB: Three concentric circles (Cities inside Districts, Districts inside States)
questions.optionC: Two intersecting circles inside a third circle
questions.explanation: A city is located within a district, and a district is located within a state. Hence, Cities is a subset of Districts, which is a subset of States. This represents three concentric circles.

questions.questionText: In a competitive exam of 200 candidates, 110 passed Quantitative Aptitude, 120 passed Logical Reasoning, and 50 passed both sections. How many candidates failed both sections?
questions.explanation: Passed at least one section: n(Q union L) = n(Q) + n(L) - n(Q intersect L) = 110 + 120 - 50 = 180. Failed both sections = 200 - 180 = 20 candidates.

questions.questionText: Which Venn diagram best illustrates the relationship among: "Birds", "Bats", and "Owls"?
questions.optionA: A large circle containing two intersecting circles
questions.optionD: A large circle (Birds) containing a smaller circle (Owls), with a completely separate circle outside (Bats)
questions.explanation: Owls are birds (Owls is a subset of Birds). Bats are mammals that fly (not birds), so Bats is completely disjoint from Birds and Owls.

questions.questionText: In a housing society of 150 residents, 90 subscribe to Newspaper A, 70 subscribe to Newspaper B, and 30 subscribe to neither. How many residents subscribe ONLY to Newspaper B?
questions.explanation: Residents subscribing to at least one paper = 150 - 30 = 120. Formula: 120 = 90 + 70 - Both => Both = 160 - 120 = 40. Subscribing ONLY to Newspaper B = Total B - Both = 70 - 40 = 30 residents.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Professors", "Researchers", and "Scientists"?
questions.optionB: Three mutually intersecting circles overlapping in a central region
questions.optionC: One circle containing two disjoint circles
questions.explanation: A person can be both a professor and a researcher, a researcher and a scientist, or all three simultaneously. Thus, three mutually intersecting circles best represents the relationship.

questions.questionText: In a software company, 60 engineers work on Frontend, 55 work on Backend, and 25 work on both. If 10 engineers work on neither, how many total engineers are in the company?
questions.explanation: Total working on at least one = Frontend + Backend - Both = 60 + 55 - 25 = 90 engineers. Total engineers = 90 + 10 (neither) = 100 engineers.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Vegetables", "Potatoes", and "Apples"?
questions.optionC: A large circle containing both Potatoes and Apples intersecting each other
questions.optionD: A large circle (Vegetables) containing Potatoes, with Apples as a separate disjoint circle
questions.explanation: Potato is a vegetable (subset of Vegetables). Apple is a fruit, completely separate from vegetables. Thus, Vegetables contains Potatoes, and Apples is a disjoint circle outside.

questions.questionText: In a batch of 90 students, 40 study French, 35 study Spanish, and 15 study both languages. How many students study Spanish but NOT French?
questions.explanation: Students studying Spanish but NOT French = Total Spanish - Both = 35 - 15 = 20 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Earth", "Planets", and "Moon"?
questions.optionB: A large circle (Planets) containing Earth, with Moon as an independent disjoint circle outside
questions.optionD: A circle containing both Earth and Moon
questions.explanation: Earth is a planet (subset of Planets). The Moon is a natural satellite, not a planet. Thus, Planets contains Earth, and Moon is a disjoint circle.

questions.questionText: In a gym of 75 members, 45 lift weights, 30 do cardio, and 10 do neither. How many members do BOTH weights and cardio?
questions.explanation: Members doing at least one = 75 - 10 = 65. Weights + Cardio - Both = 65 => 45 + 30 - Both = 65 => 75 - Both = 65 => Both = 10 members.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Tables", "Chairs", and "Furniture"?
questions.optionD: A large circle (Furniture) enclosing two separate non-overlapping circles (Tables and Chairs)
questions.explanation: Both Tables and Chairs belong to the broader category of Furniture, but a table is not a chair. Thus, a large circle contains two disjoint circles.

questions.questionText: In a test of 60 students, 35 passed Physics and 30 passed Chemistry. If every student passed at least one of the two subjects, how many students passed BOTH Physics and Chemistry?
questions.explanation: Since every student passed at least one: n(P union C) = 60. Formula: 60 = 35 + 30 - Both => 60 = 65 - Both => Both = 65 - 60 = 5 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Elephants", "Carnivores", and "Tigers"?
questions.optionB: A circle (Carnivores) containing Tigers, with Elephants completely outside as a disjoint circle
questions.optionD: Carnivores containing both Elephants and Tigers
questions.explanation: Tigers are obligate carnivores (subset of Carnivores). Elephants are herbivores (completely disjoint from Carnivores and Tigers). Hence, Carnivores contains Tigers, with Elephants separate.

questions.questionText: In an office of 110 employees, 70 drink Green Tea, 50 drink Black Tea, and 20 drink both. How many drink NEITHER Green Tea nor Black Tea?
questions.explanation: Union = 70 + 50 - 20 = 100 employees drink at least one type of tea. Neither = Total - Union = 110 - 100 = 10 employees.

questions.questionText: In a college of 200 students: 100 play Cricket, 80 play Football, and 70 play Hockey. 40 play Cricket and Football, 30 play Football and Hockey, 35 play Cricket and Hockey, and 15 play all three sports. How many students play at least one of these three sports?
questions.explanation: Formula: n(A union B union C) = n(A) + n(B) + n(C) - n(AB) - n(BC) - n(AC) + n(ABC) = 100 + 80 + 70 - 40 - 30 - 35 + 15 = 250 - 105 + 15 = 160 students.

questions.questionText: In a cohort of 100 engineering students: 50 know C++, 40 know Java, and 30 know Python. 20 know C++ and Java, 15 know Java and Python, 10 know C++ and Python, and 5 know all three languages. How many students know NONE of these three programming languages?
questions.explanation: At least one language: n(C union J union P) = 50 + 40 + 30 - 20 - 15 - 10 + 5 = 120 - 45 + 5 = 80 students. Students knowing none = Total - 80 = 100 - 80 = 20 students.

questions.questionText: In a market survey of 150 consumers: 80 purchase Brand A, 65 purchase Brand B, and 55 purchase Brand C. 30 purchase Brands A and B, 25 purchase Brands B and C, 20 purchase Brands A and C, and 10 purchase all three brands. How many consumers purchase ONLY Brand A?
questions.explanation: Only Brand A = Total A - (AB + AC - ABC) = 80 - (30 + 20 - 10) = 80 - 40 = 40 consumers.

questions.questionText: In a class of 80 students, 30 like Math, 35 like Science, and 40 like English. 12 like Math and Science, 15 like Science and English, 10 like Math and English, and 5 like all three subjects. How many students like EXACTLY TWO of these three subjects?
questions.explanation: In a 3-set Venn diagram, the region representing exactly two subjects is: (n(MS) - n(MSE)) + (n(SE) - n(MSE)) + (n(ME) - n(MSE)) = (12 - 5) + (15 - 5) + (10 - 5) = 7 + 10 + 5 = 22 students.

questions.questionText: In a survey of 120 music listeners: 65 listen to Rock, 55 listen to Pop, and 45 listen to Classical. 25 listen to Rock and Pop, 20 listen to Pop and Classical, 15 listen to Rock and Classical, and 10 listen to all three genres. How many listen to EXACTLY ONE genre?
questions.explanation: Only Rock = 65 - (25 + 15 - 10) = 65 - 30 = 35. Only Pop = 55 - (25 + 20 - 10) = 55 - 35 = 20. Only Classical = 45 - (20 + 15 - 10) = 45 - 25 = 20. Exactly one genre = Only Rock + Only Pop + Only Classical = 35 + 20 + 20 = 75 listeners.

questions.questionText: In a university department of 60 professors, 30 speak French, 25 speak German, and 20 speak Russian. 10 speak French and German, 8 speak German and Russian, 7 speak French and Russian, and 3 speak all three languages. How many professors speak French and German but NOT Russian?
questions.explanation: French and German but NOT Russian corresponds directly to the region (French intersect German) minus all three: n(F intersect G) - n(F intersect G intersect R) = 10 - 3 = 7 professors.

questions.questionText: In a residential society of 200 residents: 110 read English newspaper, 90 read Hindi newspaper, and 60 read Regional newspaper. 40 read English and Hindi, 30 read Hindi and Regional, 25 read English and Regional, and 15 read all three. How many residents read ONLY the Hindi newspaper?
questions.explanation: Only Hindi = Total Hindi - (Hindi & English + Hindi & Regional - All three) = 90 - (40 + 30 - 15) = 90 - 55 = 35 residents.

questions.questionText: A sports academy has 100 athletes. 48 train in Swimming, 45 in Running, and 40 in Cycling. 18 do Swimming and Running, 15 do Running and Cycling, 12 do Swimming and Cycling, and 5 do all three. How many athletes train in NEITHER of these three sports?

In a group of 50 students, 28 like Chocolate ice cream, 24 like Vanilla, and 20 like Strawberry. 10 like Chocolate and Vanilla, 8 like Vanilla and Strawberry, 7 like Chocolate and Strawberry, and 4 like all three. How many students like Chocolate and Strawberry but NOT Vanilla?
questions.explanation: The region liking Chocolate and Strawberry without Vanilla is n(C intersect S) - n(C intersect V intersect S) = 7 - 4 = 3 students.

questions.questionText: In a library, 70 visitors read Fiction, 50 read Non-Fiction, and 40 read Science. 20 read Fiction and Non-Fiction, 15 read Non-Fiction and Science, 12 read Fiction and Science, and 8 read all three. How many visitors read Science but NEITHER Fiction NOR Non-Fiction?
questions.explanation: Only Science = Total Science - (Fiction & Science + Non-Fiction & Science - All three) = 40 - (12 + 15 - 8) = 40 - 19 = 21 visitors.

questions.questionText: In an exam taken by 150 students, 90 passed Mathematics, 80 passed Physics, and 75 passed Chemistry. 45 passed Math and Physics, 40 passed Physics and Chemistry, 35 passed Math and Chemistry, and 20 passed all three. How many students failed in ALL three subjects?
questions.explanation: Passed at least one = 90 + 80 + 75 - 45 - 40 - 35 + 20 = 245 - 120 + 20 = 145 students. Failed all three = 150 - 145 = 5 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Professions", "Architects", and "Civil Engineers"?
questions.optionA: A large circle (Professions) containing two intersecting circles (Architects and Civil Engineers)
questions.optionD: Professions containing two separate disjoint circles
questions.explanation: Both Architects and Civil Engineers are Professions (subsets of Professions). Some people hold qualifications in both architecture and civil engineering (dual-degree professionals). Thus, a large circle encloses two intersecting circles.

questions.questionText: In a tech incubator of 90 founders, 50 have technical backgrounds, 45 have business backgrounds, and 35 have design backgrounds. 20 have both tech and business, 15 have business and design, 12 have tech and design, and 5 have all three. How many founders have ONLY a design background?
questions.explanation: Only design = Total Design - (Tech & Design + Business & Design - All three) = 35 - (12 + 15 - 5) = 35 - 22 = 13 founders.

questions.questionText: In a sample of 250 voters: 130 favor Policy A, 110 favor Policy B, and 95 favor Policy C. 55 favor A and B, 45 favor B and C, 40 favor A and C, and 20 favor all three. How many voters favor at least one of the three policies?
questions.explanation: At least one policy: n(A union B union C) = 130 + 110 + 95 - 55 - 45 - 40 + 20 = 335 - 140 + 20 = 215 voters.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best illustrates: "Reptiles", "Snakes", and "Lizards"?
questions.optionC: A large circle (Reptiles) enclosing two separate non-overlapping circles (Snakes and Lizards)
questions.explanation: Snakes and Lizards are both Reptiles, but no snake is a lizard (distinct suborders Serpentes and Lacertilia). Thus, an enclosing circle contains two disjoint circles.

questions.questionText: In a club of 70 members, 35 play Chess, 30 play Scrabble, and 25 play Bridge. 12 play Chess and Scrabble, 10 play Scrabble and Bridge, 8 play Chess and Bridge, and 4 play all three. How many members play EXACTLY TWO games?
questions.explanation: Exactly two games = (Chess&Scrabble - All) + (Scrabble&Bridge - All) + (Chess&Bridge - All) = (12 - 4) + (10 - 4) + (8 - 4) = 8 + 6 + 4 = 18 members.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Quadrilaterals", "Rectangles", and "Squares"?
questions.optionA: Three concentric circles with Squares inside Rectangles, and Rectangles inside Quadrilaterals
questions.optionC: A circle containing two separate circles
questions.explanation: All squares are rectangles, and all rectangles are quadrilaterals. This forms a strict chain of subset inclusion, represented by three concentric circles.

questions.questionText: In a hospital staff of 80 nurses, 40 have ICU certification, 35 have ER certification, and 30 have Pediatric certification. 15 have ICU & ER, 12 have ER & Pediatric, 10 have ICU & Pediatric, and 5 have all three certifications. How many nurses have ONLY ICU certification?
questions.explanation: Only ICU = Total ICU - (ICU & ER + ICU & Pediatric - All three) = 40 - (15 + 10 - 5) = 40 - 20 = 20 nurses.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Liquids", "Water", and "Oil"?
questions.optionC: A large circle (Liquids) enclosing two disjoint circles (Water and Oil)
questions.explanation: Both Water and Oil are liquids, but water is not oil (immiscible, chemically distinct). A large circle contains two non-overlapping circles.

questions.questionText: In a test batch of 100 components, 45 passed Stress Test, 40 passed Temperature Test, and 35 passed Vibration Test. 15 passed Stress & Temp, 12 passed Temp & Vibration, 10 passed Stress & Vibration, and 4 passed all three. How many components passed Temperature and Vibration tests but FAILED the Stress test?
questions.explanation: Passed Temperature and Vibration but not Stress = (Temp intersect Vibration) - All three = 12 - 4 = 8 components.

questions.questionText: In an international summit of 120 delegates: 70 speak English, 60 speak French, and 50 speak Spanish. 30 speak English and French, 25 speak French and Spanish, 20 speak English and Spanish, and 10 speak all three languages. How many delegates speak EXACTLY ONE of these three languages?
questions.explanation: Only English = 70 - (30 + 20 - 10) = 70 - 40 = 30. Only French = 60 - (30 + 25 - 10) = 60 - 45 = 15. Only Spanish = 50 - (25 + 20 - 10) = 50 - 35 = 15. Exactly one language = 30 + 15 + 15 = 60 delegates. Wait: let us check option: "60". Correct: 60.

questions.questionText: In a corporate survey, out of 300 employees: 180 use Slack, 140 use Teams, and 100 use Zoom. 80 use Slack and Teams, 50 use Teams and Zoom, 40 use Slack and Zoom, and 20 use all three tools. How many employees use AT LEAST TWO of these communication tools?
questions.explanation: At least two tools = (Slack&Teams only) + (Teams&Zoom only) + (Slack&Zoom only) + All three = (80 - 20) + (50 - 20) + (40 - 20) + 20 = 60 + 30 + 20 + 20 = 130 employees.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Fathers", "Males", and "Engineers"?
questions.optionB: A circle of Males completely containing Fathers, with Engineers intersecting both Males and Fathers
questions.optionD: Males and Fathers intersecting outside Engineers
questions.explanation: All fathers are biologically males (Fathers is a strict subset of Males). Some engineers are fathers, some engineers are males who are not fathers, and some engineers are females (neither fathers nor males). Thus, Engineers intersects both Males and the inner Fathers circle.

questions.questionText: In a school of 200 students: 120 participate in Music, 100 in Dance, and 80 in Drama. 50 in Music & Dance, 40 in Dance & Drama, 35 in Music & Drama, and 20 in all three. How many students participate in NONE of these three activities?

In a company of 80 employees: 42 drink Tea, 38 drink Coffee, and 30 drink Juice. 16 drink Tea and Coffee, 14 drink Coffee and Juice, 12 drink Tea and Juice, and 6 drink all three. How many drink Tea and Juice but NOT Coffee?
questions.explanation: Tea and Juice but NOT Coffee = n(Tea intersect Juice) - n(Tea intersect Coffee intersect Juice) = 12 - 6 = 6 employees.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Polygons", "Triangles", and "Scalene Triangles"?
questions.optionA: Three concentric circles (Scalene Triangles inside Triangles, Triangles inside Polygons)
questions.explanation: Every scalene triangle is a triangle, and every triangle is a polygon. This represents three concentric circles.

questions.questionText: In an algorithm test taken by 100 students: 60 solved Problem 1, 50 solved Problem 2, and 45 solved Problem 3. 25 solved Problems 1 & 2, 20 solved Problems 2 & 3, 15 solved Problems 1 & 3, and 5 solved all three problems. How many students solved ONLY Problem 1?
questions.explanation: Only Problem 1 = Total Problem 1 - (1&2 + 1&3 - All three) = 60 - (25 + 15 - 5) = 60 - 35 = 25 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Lawyers", "Females", and "Mothers"?
questions.optionC: A circle of Females completely containing Mothers, with Lawyers intersecting both Females and Mothers
questions.explanation: All mothers are females (Mothers is a subset of Females). Some lawyers are mothers, some lawyers are females who are not mothers, and some lawyers are males (outside Females). Thus, Lawyers intersects both Females and the subset Mothers.

questions.questionText: In a consumer study of 150 gadget owners: 85 own a Tablet, 75 own a Laptop, and 60 own a Smartwatch. 35 own Tablet & Laptop, 25 own Laptop & Smartwatch, 20 own Tablet & Smartwatch, and 10 own all three gadgets. How many own a Laptop and Smartwatch but NOT a Tablet?
questions.explanation: Laptop and Smartwatch without Tablet = (Laptop intersect Smartwatch) - All three = 25 - 10 = 15 owners.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Currency", "Yen", and "Euro"?
questions.optionA: A large circle (Currency) containing two separate non-overlapping circles (Yen and Euro)
questions.explanation: Both Yen and Euro are currencies (subsets of Currency), but Yen is not Euro (distinct currencies). Thus, an enclosing circle contains two disjoint circles.

questions.questionText: In an audit of 160 tax filings: 90 claimed Deduction A, 80 claimed Deduction B, and 70 claimed Deduction C. 40 claimed A & B, 30 claimed B & C, 25 claimed A & C, and 15 claimed all three. How many tax filings claimed EXACTLY ONE deduction?
Which diagram represents: "Atmospheric Gases", "Oxygen", and "Nitrogen"?
questions.optionC: A large circle (Atmospheric Gases) containing two separate non-overlapping circles (Oxygen and Nitrogen)
questions.explanation: Both Oxygen and Nitrogen are atmospheric gases, but Oxygen is chemically distinct from Nitrogen. Thus, an enclosing circle contains two disjoint circles.

questions.questionText: In an e-commerce platform survey of 120 shoppers: 65 bought Clothing, 50 bought Footwear, and 45 bought Accessories. 25 bought Clothing & Footwear, 20 bought Footwear & Accessories, 15 bought Clothing & Accessories, and 8 bought all three categories. How many shoppers bought AT LEAST ONE of these three categories?
Which diagram best represents: "Animals", "Herbivores", and "Deer"?
questions.optionA: Three concentric circles (Deer inside Herbivores, Herbivores inside Animals)
questions.explanation: All deer are herbivores, and all herbivores are animals. This represents three concentric circles.

questions.questionText: In a tournament of 100 chess players: 55 know the Sicilian Defense, 45 know the French Defense, and 35 know the Caro-Kann Defense. 20 know Sicilian & French, 15 know French & Caro-Kann, 10 know Sicilian & Caro-Kann, and 5 know all three openings. How many players know EXACTLY TWO openings?
questions.explanation: Exactly two openings = (20 - 5) + (15 - 5) + (10 - 5) = 15 + 10 + 5 = 30 players.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Planets", "Mars", and "Jupiter"?
questions.optionC: A large circle (Planets) enclosing two separate non-overlapping circles (Mars and Jupiter)
questions.explanation: Both Mars and Jupiter are planets, but Mars is distinct from Jupiter. A large enclosing circle contains two disjoint circles.

questions.questionText: In an academic batch of 80 students: 40 like Algebra, 35 like Geometry, and 30 like Calculus. 15 like Algebra & Geometry, 12 like Geometry & Calculus, 10 like Algebra & Calculus, and 5 like all three. How many students like Algebra and Calculus but NOT Geometry?
questions.explanation: Algebra and Calculus without Geometry = (Algebra intersect Calculus) - All three = 10 - 5 = 5 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram best represents: "Writers", "Poets", and "Novelist"?
questions.optionA: A large circle (Writers) containing two intersecting circles (Poets and Novelists)
questions.explanation: Poets and Novelists are both Writers (subsets of Writers). Some writers write both poetry and novels (intersection). Thus, Writers encloses two intersecting circles.

questions.questionText: In a test of 90 students: 50 passed Section A, 45 passed Section B, and 40 passed Section C. 20 passed A & B, 15 passed B & C, 12 passed A & C, and 5 passed all three. How many students passed ONLY Section B?
questions.explanation: Only Section B = Total B - (AB + BC - ABC) = 45 - (20 + 15 - 5) = 45 - 30 = 15 students.

questions.questionText: Which diagram represents: "Automobiles", "Sedans", and "SUVs"?
questions.optionC: A large circle (Automobiles) enclosing two separate non-overlapping circles (Sedans and SUVs)
questions.explanation: Both Sedans and SUVs are Automobiles, but a sedan is not an SUV (distinct vehicle body types). An enclosing circle contains two disjoint circles.
